name: Natchez Trace Inn-to-Inn: Jackson to Natchez

overview: Six days, five nights, four towns. You ride south from Jackson to Natchez on the Natchez Trace Parkway and the quiet state and county roads between. Every night is in a historic inn.
You sleep in Vicksburg for two nights, at Canemount in Lorman for one, and in Natchez for two. Both layover days are short on purpose: the Vicksburg battlefield loop and a free day in Natchez.
at_a_glance: 6 days, 5 nights, plus a Sunday night in Jackson before you start
Est. 150-190 miles, depending on the options you take
Inn chain: linear, with two layover towns
Inn-to-inn riders and e-bike riders (with charging checks)
Moderate. Riding days of roughly 40-60 miles, layover days 0-30
Paved throughout. About half on the Natchez Trace Parkway, half on state and county roads
public.direction: South. You ride out of Jackson through Clinton to the Trace, on to Vicksburg, then down to Natchez. Winds generally favor riding north, so expect some headwind days. The payoff is finishing in Natchez.
public.why_sunday: Sunday to Saturday avoids the two weak spots. The Enterprise office in Natchez is closed Sundays, which rules out a Sunday one-way rental home, and Vicksburg has few dinner options on Sunday nights. It also puts the Trace days on weekdays, when traffic is lighter.
public.bad_hour: Somewhere on your second day in the saddle, usually a dozen or so miles in, you hit a low patch. Legs heavy, head asking why you signed up. It passes. Eat something, drink something, keep turning the pedals.
public.best_months: March to April and October. Book inns 6 to 8 weeks ahead for those months. Canemount has only six rooms. July and August are hot and humid. Spring brings rain, so carry a real rain jacket.
day_summaries: Ride out through Clinton to the Trace, south to MS 27, then west into Vicksburg. Est. 50-60 miles.
Vicksburg layover. The 16-mile National Military Park loop, or no bike at all.
Vicksburg to Port Gibson and Windsor Ruins, then Canemount at Lorman. The longest day. Est. 45-60 miles.
Canemount to Natchez. Thirty miles of the best road on the Trace, ending at the parkway's southern terminus. Est. 44 miles.
Natchez layover. Walk the bluff, or ride a loop of up to 30 miles.
Home from Natchez by air, one-way rental, or pre-booked van.

faq.q: How long is the Natchez Trace Inn-to-Inn tour from Jackson to Natchez?
faq.a: Six days and five nights, plus a Sunday night in Jackson before you start. The riding is an estimated 150-190 miles, depending on the options you take. Riding days run roughly 40-60 miles. Days 2 and 5 are layovers.

faq.q: Why start on a Sunday and finish on a Saturday?
faq.a: The Enterprise office in Natchez is closed Sundays, which rules out a Sunday one-way rental home, and Vicksburg has few dinner options on Sunday nights. Sunday to Saturday also puts the Trace days on weekdays, when traffic is lighter.

faq.q: Is the whole route on the Natchez Trace Parkway?
faq.a: No. About half is on the parkway and half is on state and county roads. Everything is paved. The parkway has a 50 mph limit, 11-foot lanes and no shoulder. The state roads are a mix, and the tour page flags the stretches where the shoulder or traffic is unconfirmed.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to ride it?
faq.a: March to April and October. Summer heat and humidity make July and August hard going, and spring brings rain. Book inns 6 to 8 weeks ahead for the good months, because Canemount has only six rooms.

faq.q: How do I get home from Natchez?
faq.a: Fly out of Natchez to Houston, pick up an Enterprise one-way rental to Jackson airport by noon on Saturday, or book a van ahead. Greyhound to Baton Rouge and shipping your bike home are the other options. The tour page lists each one with phone numbers and costs.

faq.q: Can I ride it on an e-bike?
faq.a: Yes, with planning. Day 3 is the range test, with up to 60 miles of rolling terrain. Charge fully in Vicksburg and ask Canemount about an outlet for overnight charging. Vicksburg National Military Park allows e-bikes under 750W, but not riding on the motor alone.

faq.q: Is there luggage transfer between inns?
faq.a: Not confirmed for this route. Until one is found, plan to carry your own gear in panniers or a trunk bag, or have a friend drive it.

faq.q: Can I camp instead of staying in inns?
faq.a: Camping is thin on this route. Natchez State Park has tent sites about 10 miles north of town, and Rocky Springs has no drinkable water. This tour is built around inns. A camping version needs its own chain of stops.

faq.q: How much does a self-guided Natchez Trace tour cost?
faq.a: It depends on where you sleep. Camping keeps it low; inn-to-inn with historic B&Bs runs roughly $150-260 a night per room. Add food, getting to the start in Jackson, and getting home from Natchez. Access to this page includes every inn with its price range.

Somewhere on your second day in the saddle, usually a dozen or so miles in, you hit a low patch. Legs heavy, head asking why you signed up. It passes. Eat something, drink something, keep turning the pedals.

map.note: The Trace part of today's ride. Mileposts are approximate. The rest is city streets and MS 27.

days.title: Ride out through Clinton to the Trace, then on to Vicksburg
route: Ride out of Jackson through Clinton to the Natchez Trace at the Clinton Visitor Center (MP 89). That is about 10 miles on city and suburban streets. Then ride south on the Trace to the MS 27 exit (MP 67), and west about 20 miles on MS 27 into Vicksburg.
The Trace section rolls gently, with a maximum grade of about 3.6%. This is your first taste of the parkway: no trucks, no billboards, 11-foot lanes.
Prefer to skip the city miles? A taxi van or a Jackson bike shop may shuttle you to the Clinton Visitor Center (MP 89). Call ahead to confirm.
road_notes: The city and suburban streets between Jackson and Clinton are the busiest miles of the day.
The Trace is smooth, with no shoulder.
MS 27 turns four-lane undivided near Beechwood as you come into Vicksburg.
days.lunch: Pack it. The Trace has no food. Raymond sits about 2 miles off the parkway near MP 78.
days.dinner: Walnut Hills (open Monday, closed Tuesday) or Restaurant Anchuca (Mon 5-7:30). The restaurant at Cedar Grove is closed Mondays, but its bar is open.
days.water: Fill bottles at the inn. The Clinton Visitor Center (MP 89) has water.
warnings: If you do shuttle, an UberXL will not reliably take bikes. You need a van or a car with a bike rack.

days.title: Vicksburg layover
route: The Vicksburg National Military Park tour road is a 16-mile loop through the siege lines, with shorter 3 to 16 mile options. It is hilly in short bursts, and traffic on the tour road can be heavy at times.
road_notes: Ride with traffic, inside the white line.
No riding on monuments or through Thayer's Approach tunnel.
days.breakfast: At the inn, or Bohemia Cafe & Bakery downtown (Mon-Fri 7-noon).
days.lunch: Downtown: Rusty's Riverfront Grill (Tue-Fri 11-1:30). Walnut Hills is closed Tuesdays.
days.snacks: No food is confirmed inside the park. Carry snacks.
days.dinner: Rusty's, 10 South Rooftop (Tue-Thu 5-9), or Cedar Grove (Tue-Sat, by reservation).
days.water: No water is confirmed inside the park. Carry it.
warnings: The park fee is $10 per cyclist, good for 7 days. Card only, no cash.
The section near the Illinois Memorial (tour stops 2 and 3) has been closed since March 2026, with no reopening date.

days.title: Vicksburg to Canemount via Port Gibson and Windsor Ruins
route: The longest day, and the least settled. There are two ways to Port Gibson.
Option 1: back along MS 27 and down the Trace, an est. 57-62 miles total. It is quieter and prettier, and passes Rocky Springs and the Sunken Trace. It is also long.
Option 2: US 61 south, an est. 42-47 miles total. It is shorter, but it is mostly a four-lane divided highway. Not recommended until someone has ridden or driven it.
From Port Gibson, MS 552 (Rodney Road) is a quiet two-lane to Windsor Ruins, the 23 columns left of an 1861 mansion. Canemount is about 2 miles north of Alcorn State on the same road.
road_notes: MS 552 from Port Gibson to Windsor Ruins and Canemount is quiet two-lane road.
days.breakfast: At the inn. Cedar Grove's hot breakfast suits an early start.
days.lunch: Old Country Store in Lorman, a buffet listed daily 10am-4pm. Call 601-437-3661 to confirm. If you are running late, do not count on it.
days.snacks: Shell station on Hwy 61 in Port Gibson (open 24 hours).
days.dinner: Only at Canemount, and only if you arrange it when you book. Otherwise carry dinner from Port Gibson or the Old Country Store. There is no restaurant within about 17 miles.
days.water: Fill up in Vicksburg and Port Gibson. Windsor Ruins has no water and no restrooms.
side_trips: Windsor Ruins, open dawn to dusk.
Grand Gulf Military Park, about 8 miles northwest of Port Gibson ($4). It adds roughly 16 miles round trip, so it suits only a strong rider on the shorter US 61 route.
warnings: If you skip the Old Country Store, you are carrying dinner and lunch.
unconfirmed: Shoulder and truck traffic on US 61.
Dinner for cyclists at Canemount, and the breakfast time (601-940-7206).

map.note: The Trace part of today's ride. Mileposts are approximate. You join the Trace at MP 30 from MS 552 and finish about 2.5 miles into town.

days.title: Canemount to Natchez
route: The best Trace day of the tour. Seven miles east on MS 552 (the first 5 from Alcorn have a wide shoulder) to the Trace at MP 30. Then 30 miles south to the end of the parkway, and about 2.5 miles into town.
The road rolls, with about 1,800 feet of climbing.
road_notes: Coles Creek (MP 17.5) has restrooms and a bike repair station.
Mount Locust (MP 15.5): the old inn building is closed for structural repairs. The grounds are open.
days.lunch: Pack a lunch. There is no food on the Trace between Lorman and Natchez. For a late lunch in Natchez, try The Camp on Silver Street (daily 11-8) or Magnolia Grill (closed Mondays only).
days.dinner: The Castle at Dunleith (Thursday 6-9) or Fat Mama's Tamales downtown.
side_trips: Emerald Mound, 1 mile west on MS 553 at MP 10.3. It adds 2 miles. Go, everyone: it is the second-largest ceremonial mound in the country.
warnings: No food on the Trace between Lorman and Natchez.

days.title: Natchez layover
route: A rest day in a town built for walking, with an optional ride.
The ride: a loop of about 30 miles combining the Trace and the Mississippi River Trail, with about 950 feet of climbing. Or an easy spin on downtown streets and the bluff trail.
Off the bike: antebellum homes, the river bluff, and the Natchez Museum of African American History and Culture.
days.lunch: The Camp, Magnolia Grill, or Fat Mama's Tamales.
days.dinner: The Castle at Dunleith (Friday 6-10), The Camp, Magnolia Grill, or Fat Mama's Tamales.

days.title: Home
route: Fly out of Natchez to Houston, pick up an Enterprise one-way by noon (Saturday hours are 9 to noon), or take a pre-booked van. See Getting there and getting home.
warnings: The Enterprise office in Natchez closes at noon on Saturday.

lodging.intro: Every stop has a historic inn with recent reviews, and Canemount is the only option in Lorman, so it anchors the whole tour. Ask every inn about bike storage when you book. None of them lists it.

stops.name: Old Capitol Inn
stops.backup: Fairview Inn ($263-442). Its restaurant has no Sunday dinner.

stops.name: The Inn at Cedar Grove
stops.dinner: On site Tue-Sat by reservation. Bar daily.
stops.maps_query: Cedar Grove Mansion Inn, Vicksburg, MS
stops.backup: The Corners Mansion Inn ($181-197). Breakfast is not until 9:00, too late for Day 3.
stops.note: Cedar Grove reopened under new owners in April 2025.

stops.name: Canemount Plantation Inn
stops.dinner: Only if you arrange it with the inn. No restaurant within about 17 miles.
stops.backup: None. There is nothing else in Lorman.
stops.note: Book direct by phone or the inn's reservation page. It is not on Booking.com. Six rooms, no children under 14.

stops.name: Dunleith Historic Inn
stops.backup: Natchez Grand Hotel ($111-248), on the bluff, walking distance to 19 restaurants.

lodging.budget: Budget options: Hampton Inn & Suites across from the Vicksburg battlefield entrance ($140-236) and Hampton Inn & Suites Natchez, walkable to downtown ($154-284).
lodging.camping: Camping is thin on this route. Natchez State Park has tent sites about 10 miles north of town, Rocky Springs has no drinkable water, and the Vicksburg campground is not worth recommending. A camping version of this tour needs its own chain.

items.title: Fly into Jackson (JAN)
items.body: Nonstops from Atlanta, Charlotte, Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Nashville and Washington Reagan, among others.

items.title: Airport to your inn
items.body: About 6 miles. With a bike box, book an UberXL (about $25) or a taxi. No inn shuttles found.

items.title: Ship your bike instead
items.body: The Bike Crossing in Ridgeland is listed as assembling bikes and delivering to area hotels. Call 601-856-0049 to confirm. No touring or e-bike rentals are confirmed in Jackson.

items.title: Driving in
items.body: The airport long-term lot is $13/day, about $78 for the week, with a shuttle. Inn parking for a full week is unconfirmed.

getting_home.intro: The return from Natchez is the hard part. The cyclist shuttle riders used to rely on appears to have stopped running in September 2025.

options.notes: Daily United Express to Houston since July 2026. These are 50-seat jets, so check bike-box limits.
The only rental company in Natchez. Mon-Fri 8-5, Sat 9-noon, closed Sunday. Small fleet, so book early. Phone 601-442-4600.
Runs to airports within 200 miles. Ask about bikes. Phone 601-334-2183.

options.option: Greyhound to Baton Rouge, then fly
options.notes: One bus a day. Bikes must be boxed.
Natchez Bicycle is listed as packing and shipping bikes. Phone 601-392-2070.

getting_home.notes: Baton Rouge airport (BTR) is about 85 miles from Natchez, roughly the same as Jackson. There is no Amtrak in Natchez. The nearest station, Brookhaven, is about 65 miles away.

conditions.road_status: The lower Trace (MP 0-100) had no road closures as of the National Park Service update of August 14, 2026. The current closures (MP 135-159.5 and the Double Arch Bridge) are well north of this tour.
season: Best months: March to April and October. Book inns 6 to 8 weeks ahead for those months. Canemount has only six rooms.
Avoid July and August. Heat and humidity make it hard going.
Spring brings rain. Carry a real rain jacket.
on_the_trace: 50 mph speed limit, 11-foot lanes, no shoulder. Ride single file, wear bright colors and run lights. Cyclists may use the full lane.
Groups of 8 or more may need a National Park Service permit, requested 10 business days ahead.

ebike: Vicksburg's tour road allows e-bikes under 750W, but not riding on the motor alone.
Day 3 is the range test: up to 60 miles with rolling terrain and gear. Charge fully in Vicksburg, and ask Canemount about an outlet for overnight charging.
Natchez Bicycle lists e-bikes for rent (4 listed) if you would rather not travel with one. Phone 601-392-2070.
luggage: No luggage-transfer service is confirmed for this route. Wynn Transportation (601-334-2183) is the lead to ask.
Until one is found, this tour is carry-your-own: panniers, a trunk bag, or a friend with a car.
